No, not all of it. Of the 81.3 ha of 2021 tree-cover loss (2.23% of the asset), the MGAP 2021 forest map places about 68.1 ha in planted forest (Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda). Roughly 13.2 ha falls outside any mapped forest, and no loss is in native forest. So about 84% was in the plantation and about 16% was not.

Two caveats:
- Hansen also detected a further 37.3 ha of loss in patches under 0.5 ha. These aren't counted as events, so they aren't in the 81.3 ha and weren't classified by forest type.
- The evidence shows tree-cover loss only. It doesn't establish whether this was deforestation, such as plantation harvest versus land-use change, or what caused it. It also doesn't show whether it was authorized, who was responsible, or any compliance status.

The loss is corroborated: a later year was observed, and the JRC 2020 forest reference agrees on 98% of the event area.
